value.overview: The Yellow-bellied Elaenia (Elaenia flavogaster) is a small, active tyrant flycatcher of the American tropics. It is recognizable by its bushy crest, olive-green upperparts, pale wing bars, grayish head and breast, and yellowish belly. Unlike many flycatchers, it commonly uses gardens, farmland, scrub, forest edges, and other open habitats. It often perches conspicuously while making short flights to catch insects or take small fruits.
value.classification: The Yellow-bellied Elaenia belongs to the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers, and the genus Elaenia. Its scientific name is Elaenia flavogaster.
value.identification: This medium-small flycatcher has olive-green upperparts, a grayish head and throat, a whitish or pale eye ring, and two pale wing bars. The underparts are grayish on the breast and yellow on the belly and undertail coverts. Its bushy crest is a useful feature, although it may be held flat. The bill is broad and dark, and the wings and tail are relatively plain. Its emphatic, somewhat harsh calls are often easier to detect than the bird itself.
value.rangeHabitat: The species ranges from southern Mexico through Central America and across much of northern and eastern South America, with additional populations in parts of the Caribbean. In Costa Rica, it is a resident species found widely from the lowlands into the highlands, locally reaching about 1,850–2,200 meters. It is generally associated with secondary growth, scrub, open woodland, forest edges, clearings, gardens, plantations, parks, and other habitats with scattered trees. It avoids the interior of dense, continuous forest.
value.migrationStatus: The Yellow-bellied Elaenia is generally resident in Costa Rica and does not undertake a regular long-distance migration there. Local or seasonal movements may occur, especially in response to food availability or rainfall, but Costa Rican birds are present throughout the year.
value.breeding: The Yellow-bellied Elaenia usually nests in an open cup built from plant fibers and other fine materials, placed on a branch or in a small tree or shrub. Breeding pairs defend a territory and may nest in disturbed habitats as well as along forest edges. The female performs most incubation, while both adults participate in feeding the young. Nesting timing varies across its broad range and is linked to local rainfall and food conditions.
value.dietFeeding: Its diet consists mainly of insects and other small arthropods, supplemented by small fruits and occasionally seeds. It commonly waits from a perch and makes short sallies to seize flying insects or pluck items from foliage. In Costa Rica it frequently feeds in the middle levels of shrubs and trees, and it may visit fruiting plants in gardens, secondary vegetation, and forest margins.
value.behavior: The Yellow-bellied Elaenia is alert, active, and usually encountered singly or in pairs rather than in large flocks. It often sits upright on an exposed perch, repeatedly calling and making brief flights through nearby vegetation. Individuals may defend territories throughout the year. Its tolerance of gardens, farms, and regenerating woodland allows it to live close to people, where its loud calls can reveal its presence before it is seen.

conservation.populationTrend: The global population is considered stable.
